sources.IRC103_2012_6.2.1: IRC:103-2012 cl 6.2.1: pavement max 150 mm above road (verified, research/claude/VERIFY-STANDARDS.md)
sources.IRC103_2022_6.7: IRC:103-2022 cl 6.7 Fig 48: kerb ramp not steeper than 1:15, flares 1:10 (verified, VERIFY-STANDARDS.md)
sources.HG2021_3.7.2: MoHUA Harmonised Guidelines 2021 cl 3.7.2: kerb ramp max 1:12 (verified, VERIFY-STANDARDS.md)
sources.HG2021_3.7.3: MoHUA HG 2021 cl 3.7.3: kerb ramp min width 900 mm (verified)
sources.HG2021_3.5.1: MoHUA HG 2021 cl 3.5.1: walkway min 1200 mm, 1800 mm two-way, 1500 mm around trees/poles (verified)
sources.UK_IM_S98: UK DfT Inclusive Mobility (FACTOR-UNIVERSE S98): thresholds over 10 mm a problem, cross-fall 2.5%, 95th pct power chair just over 700 mm wide (excerpt level)
sources.S96_crossslope: FACTOR-UNIVERSE S96 (PubMed 41945617): one-rim propulsion around 3% cross slope (excerpt level)
sources.S95_stepclimb: FACTOR-UNIVERSE S95 (PMC5672886): step-climbing power chairs median 20 cm step (excerpt level)
sources.S99_slope: FACTOR-UNIVERSE S99 (TRID 921388): perceived slope limits, >5% costly (excerpt level)
sources.GTKP_2017: GTKP IRF 2017 paper 814: Indian audit measured footpath heights 200 to 250 mm vs 150 mm standard (hermes MAX-INFO-PER-PIXEL.md)
sources.CPCB_AQI: CPCB National AQI health statements (https://cpcb.nic.in/upload/NAAQS_2019.pdf; https://cpcb.nic.in/aqi_report.php), read as search excerpts 2026-10-24: 101-200 breathing discomfort to people with lung disease such as asthma, heart disease, children, older adults; 201-300 discomfort on prolonged exposure; 301-400 respiratory illness on prolonged exposure; 401-500 affects healthy people, serious impact on lung/heart disease
sources.IMD_HEAT: IMD FAQ on heat wave (https://internal.imd.gov.in/section/nhac/dynamic/FAQ_heat_wave.pdf), search excerpt 2026-10-24: heat wave considered from 40 C plains / 30 C hills; actual max >= 45 C heat wave, >= 47 C severe
sources.NCHRP562_speeds: TCRP 112 / NCHRP 562 (https://deldot.gov/Business/drc/manuals/nchrp_rpt_562.pdf), search excerpt: mean walking speed cane or crutch 0.80 m/s, walker 0.63 m/s, wheelchair 1.08 m/s; 0.9 m/s for less capable older pedestrians
sources.AGEING_2025: Western et al., Age and Ageing 2025 (PubMed 41354090): mobility-limited older adults mean gait speed 0.77 m/s; 1.5% reach 1.2 m/s
sources.AGEING_2012: Asher et al., Age and Ageing 2012 (PubMed 22695790): UK 65+ mean walking speed 0.9 m/s men, 0.8 m/s women
sources.RPWD_SCHEDULE: RPwD Act 2016 Schedule (https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/acts_parliament/2016/Rights_of_Persons_with_Disabilities_Act_2016.pdf; Lok Sabha AU1109 list; hermes BODY-TAXONOMY.md read the Gazette text)
sources.HERMES_BODY: research/hermes/sc02/BODY-TAXONOMY.md (hermes, 2026-10-25 00:05): 61 leaves, qualitative needs; N-codes are sourced, A-cells are hermes assumptions
sources.ASSUMPTIONS_JSON: app/route/hroute/assumptions.json (existing 7-profile model): kerb block above 2 cm for wheelchairs, width 90 cm, slope 6.67%
